title: Zero units with a total cost raise an uncaught decimal.DivisionByZero
body:
A posting with zero units and a total cost divides by the unit count without guarding it, so `load_file` propagates `decimal.DivisionByZero` instead of returning an error. `bean-check` prints a traceback.

Reproduction:

```beancount
2024-01-01 open Assets:S HOOL
2024-01-01 open Assets:Cash USD

2024-02-01 * "zero units, total cost"
  Assets:S      0 HOOL {{20.00 USD}}
  Assets:Cash  -20.00 USD
```

`convert_costspec_to_cost` in `beancount/parser/booking_full.py` computes `unit_cost = cost_total / units_number` with no zero check. The `{0 # 20.00 USD}` spelling fails identically.

`load_file` is documented to return `(entries, errors, options_map)`; parse and booking problems must arrive as entries in `errors`, not as exceptions. Zero units are already guarded in `interpolate_group` (COST_PER) and handled gracefully on the `@@` total-price path.

Suggested fix: guard the division and emit a booking error for a total cost against zero units.
acceptance_criteria: load_file on a posting with `0 HOOL {{20.00 USD}}` does not raise and returns an error entry in the error list
the `{0 # 20.00 USD}` spelling of the same posting is rejected the same way
the error message states that a total cost cannot be used with zero units
compute_cost_number returns None instead of dividing when the unit count is zero
total cost with non-zero units still produces the same per-unit cost as before
no decimal.DivisionByZero escapes the loader for any cost spec form
